value.body: A cybersecurity analyst watches an organisation's systems for attacks, investigates alerts, and helps fix security weaknesses. Employers include IT services firms, banks, security operations centres, consultancies and government bodies. A typical day involves monitoring alerts, analysing logs, responding to incidents and checking systems for vulnerabilities.

items.label: Typical entry
items.value: B.Tech CSE/IT, BCA, B.Sc Computer Science or MCA

items.label: Common tools
items.value: SIEM platforms, firewalls, vulnerability scanners, Linux

items.label: Certifications
items.value: Entry-level security certifications are widely asked for

value.title: How you get in
value.body: Freshers often start as L1 analysts in a security operations centre (SOC), usually in shifts. Networking basics, Linux skills, an entry-level security certification and practice labs help in interviews.

value.title: At a glance
items: Entry SOC roles often involve night and weekend shifts.
Next roles: L2/L3 analyst, incident responder, penetration tester, security engineer.
Continuous learning is needed as threats change.
